{"label":"system_slowness","explanation":"General handle time is running about 65-100% above forecast (578-778 s vs ~370 s) since late morning, while general volume is 12-30% below forecast and attendance is normal: 2 sick against about 2.5 usual. This lines up with open incident INC-20261104-2401, opened at 11:30: knowledge-base search is timing out and agents are searching manually. Longer calls are consuming capacity on general. Demand has not risen and agents are not missing. Payments is broadly on plan, with only interval-to-interval noise.","plan_name":"General slowness containment for the rest of the day (13:15-20:00)","rationale":"Workload on general is about 60 calls per 15 min at about 650 s, roughly 43 Erlangs against about 31-32 agents on phones. The gap is large and likely lasts until the KB fix.
- Overtime: Add staff with consecutive 2-hour general offers from 13:45 to 19:45. At about 4 acceptances per offer, this costs about Rs 2,900 per block, or about Rs 11,500 including this morning's offer, which is within the Rs 15,000 budget.
- Coaching: Cancel remaining general coaching to keep agents on phones.
- Breaks: Delay early-afternoon general breaks that were not part of the morning delay.
- Demand reduction: Extend IVR callback and chat deflection (balance and offer enquiries) through end of day. No outage message is used, because this is internal slowness with no customer-facing failure.
- Cross-skilling: Payments service level has swung between 58% and 94% at its current staffing. Moving agents would risk breaching its 70% floor, so no cross-skill move is proposed.
